features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: This captures the level of formal technical education or degree attainment the letter presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: This captures direct experience designing or owning agent-based systems, especially architectures with explicit guardrails, control planes, permissions, or auditability.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: This captures whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples and design choices.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: This captures whether the applicant has actually shipped AI or LLM-backed systems in production and understands the reliability work needed to operate them responsibly.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: This captures whether the letter frames security engineering as an enabling, user-aware service for developers and internal partners rather than as policing, friction, or after-the-fact compliance.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Engineering rigor
features.description: This captures emphasis on maintainability, reliability, failure awareness, careful boundaries, and long-term operational ownership in security-sensitive systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows no clear operational or maintainer mindset.
Makes general statements about care, correctness, or seriousness.
Clearly emphasizes maintenance, failure modes, inheritability, or dependable systems.
Makes reliability thinking central, connecting it to guardrails, constraints, operational lessons, or deliberate design choices.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: This captures how consistently the letter backs claims with concrete examples, named systems, mechanisms, or other specific supporting detail.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: This captures how strongly the letter shows substantial, central Go experience in production engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: This captures whether the letter explains the observable outcomes or effects of the applicant's work rather than only listing activities or responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Narrative quality
features.description: This captures how coherent, memorable, and well-shaped the letter's overall voice, story, and flow feel beyond a bare checklist of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: This captures evidence of ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside ordinary product work, such as CTF participation or similar offensive exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: This captures responsibility for code used beyond the applicant's employer, from upstream fixes to sustained maintenance of public projects.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: This captures the technical ambition, rigor, and self-directedness of side projects or other engineering work done outside formal job responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: No independent project work is mentioned.
The letter mentions a small utility, app, or lightweight side project.
The letter shows a substantial independent technical build beyond everyday work.
The letter shows an ambitious system built to tackle hard reliability, distribution, recovery, or failure-mode problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: This captures whether the applicant is motivated by foundational platform work whose benefits compound across many teams, services, or products.

levels.descriptor: No platform-level or organization-wide leverage framing is present.
The letter expresses generic interest in scale or broad impact.
The letter explicitly frames motivation around foundational infrastructure, inherited improvements, or organization-wide leverage.

features.name: Production engineering experience
features.description: This captures the overall depth of hands-on professional software experience in real production systems, including tenure, launch history, operational ownership, and breadth of responsibility.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant depth is shown, such as just meeting the baseline or giving little evidence of repeated production ownership.
A solid but moderate track record is shown, such as a few years of experience or several launched services.
A strong track record is shown, with multiple years and repeated production launches or ownership.
An extensive track record is shown, combining multi-year experience with many launched services and clear evidence of sustained production work.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: This captures how concretely and credibly the letter establishes Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: This captures how specifically the letter explains motivation for this exact role and maps the applicant's background to the posting's particular responsibilities and requirements.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: This captures the depth of hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues, including review methods, threat analysis, and remediation follow-through.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation understanding
features.description: This captures how well the letter understands the role's core mission as scaling security work through automation, tooling, workflow design, and similar leverage mechanisms.

levels.descriptor: Does not explicitly frame security work as an automation or systems problem.
Mentions automation as useful but without a strong view of what it scales.
Clearly frames automation as a way to reduce manual security workload or extend team reach.
Shows nuanced understanding of the role as scaling scarce security expertise through systems such as triage, structured response, or variant analysis.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: This captures the strength and relevance of formal external security certifications or other third-party validation of security knowledge.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering orientation
features.description: This captures how much the letter presents the applicant as genuinely security-minded and already thinking like a security engineer rather than merely adjacent to security work.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability workflow automation
features.description: This captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No past vulnerability-handling automation is mentioned.
The letter expresses interest in this problem, but gives no concrete example of having automated it.
A concrete example of triage, intake, routing, or report-handling automation is described.
The letter shows strong end-to-end automation of vulnerability handling, with clear workflow transformation or operational value.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: This captures sentence-level professionalism and proofreading quality, including spelling, grammar, and other surface errors that affect credibility.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors, misspellings, or naming mistakes noticeably distract from the application.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the letter remains readable.
Mostly clean writing with only minor slips.
Polished, professional, and essentially error-free throughout.

other.name: Other
other.description: This groups the remaining idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly belong to one of the recurring constructs above.

levels.descriptor: Only Go is mentioned, or language breadth is unclear.
Shows Go plus one or two additional languages.
Shows Go plus several additional languages.
Shows Go plus broad multi-language experience across many systems.
